transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood), Sofia Alvarez (LyraGrid Partnerships), Derek Chan (LyraGrid Head Infra), Priya Raman (LyraGrid Product), Ethan Brooks (LyraGrid Cloud)
Links shared: partner-deck.pdf (Maya), security-onepager.pdf (Maya), lyra-baseline-traffic.csv (Ethan - promised), benchmark-spreadsheet (to be shared)

Auto-summary: quick intro, high-level architecture, agreed to run cost/latency estimates and schedule technical deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm joined by Omar and Liam, and, uh, want to do quick intros and then hear about LyraGrid's priorities.
[00:12] Sofia: Hey all, Sofia here, partnerships. Excited to explore how we might, you know, offer managed LLM inference to our customers. Derek and Ethan will cover the infra details.
[00:20] Derek: Hi, Derek. Quick note on us
LyraGrid runs multi-tenant SaaS, primarily inference workloads for recommendation and search. We operate across three regions and are evaluating partners for a managed GPU offering.
[00:32] Omar: Great, thanks. Can you give us a bit more on current stack? GPUs, k8s, cloud provider?
[00:37] Ethan: Sure. We're multi-cloud, heavy on GCP and private on-prem for certain customers. We run Kubernetes and have our own autoscaling but are evaluating both hosted and dedicated partner models. For GPUs we currently use A100s, testing some 80GB variants.
[00:50] Priya: From product perspective, SLAs for latency are critical
p95 under 150ms for token streaming on smaller chat flows
and cost needs to stay under target X per 1k requests, otherwise margin shrinks.
[01:05] Maya: Totally. At Redwood we usually discuss three integration patterns: hosted API (fastest), Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools, predictable throughput), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For LyraGrid, seems like Dedicated or Private would be the right fit given tenancy and data residency needs.
[01:20] Sofia: Yeah, data residency and KMS requirements matter
some of our enterprise customers require separate key control, HSM, audit logs.
[01:28] Liam: We support customer-managed KMS integrations, and our private control plane can be deployed into a customer VPC. There are a couple of quirks with network egress for the KV cache in some topologies but that's manageable.
[01:40] Derek: Could you expand on that KV cash
cash?
[01:47] Omar: Totally, and apologies if the auto-transcript catches it wrong
KV cache. Our runtime maintains a KV cache per session and we have policies to snapshot or share across pods for warm starts. For multi-tenant scenarios we can pin tenants to particular pools to isolate cache.
[02:02] Ethan: Nice. How do you handle kernel selection and quantization? We've seen differences across model families and sequence lengths.
[02:07] Omar: We have a compilation and kernel selection layer. It picks optimized kernels based on architecture, seq len distribution, and hardware. For customers with tight cost needs we recommend per-workload quantization profiles
sometimes 4-bit for some workloads
careful with quality regression testing.
[02:22] Priya: Right, quality monitoring and evals are a must. We run regular prompt tests. Would Redwood integrate into our eval pipeline?
[02:28] Liam: Yes, our Optimize toolkit can surface quantization and config suggestions and tie regressions to a prompt set. We can set up alerting if we detect drift.
[02:36] Sofia: From partner motion, we want to co-sell, and also offer our customers a managed inference path. What's the revenue split and go-to-market model?
[02:44] Maya: Typically we do a partner referral program and for larger deals consider channel margins. We'll share the partner program doc. Also, we often do pilots: 8-12 week POC on Dedicated or Private to validate latency and cost.
[02:56] Derek: For the pilot, we'd want example SLAs and success criteria
throughput, p95 latency, and token cost targets. Also need SOC2 and ISO docs.
[03:06] Omar: We can share SOC 2 artifacts and our security one-pager; note that auto-transcribed names may be off. We'll attach the security packet after the call.
[03:14] Ethan: On networking, VPC peering vs private link
what do you recommend for hybrid? Some of our customers are air-gapped.
[03:21] Liam: For hybrid we often push the private control plane into the customer's VPC and use direct connect-type links for on-prem. For air-gapped, we have an on-prem package. There are more ops overheads but doable.
[03:33] Sofia: Any red flags on our side
things you need from us to evaluate compatibility?
[03:38] Maya: The main artifacts: baseline traffic profile (Ethan, you mentioned CSV), target models/seq lengths, and security/compliance requirements. Also business contacts for contracting.
[03:48] Ethan: We'll share baseline today. One quick question
how do you handle graceful degradation and fallbacks when capacity crunches?
[03:55] Omar: Smart routing: route based on policy
latency, cost, region. If capacity constrained, automatic fallback to compatible model variants or burst to other regions. Can configure canary rollouts and fallback policies.
[04:08] Derek: Do you support cost breakdown per token for us to show customers?
[04:12] Liam: Yes, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards. That helps for chargeback to tenants too.
[04:20] Priya: On the integration side, how invasive is it to onboard? Can we embed SDK calls or do you prefer network-based endpoints?
[04:27] Omar: We have a simple REST/SDK interface; for private deployments it's still the same API surface. We can also provide a sidecar-like proxy if you want tighter control.
[04:35] Sofia: About timelines
if we like the pilot, what's the fastest we can go?
[04:39] Maya: For Dedicated pilot often 4 weeks to provision if capacity is available; Private can take longer depending on network and legal
typically 6-8 weeks.
[04:48] Derek: Budget
are you able to provide rough cost estimate? We need ballpark for internal approvals.
[04:52] Omar: We'll do an initial estimate based on your baseline. We'll include cost for reserved capacity and a hosted fallback.
[04:58] Priya: Any references or similar partners you've done?
[05:01] Maya: We have a few GPU partner integrations and cloud partners; we'll anonymize details but share case studies.
[05:08] Ethan: One more technical: do you support tenant isolation at the runtime level? We need strict limits for enterprise tenants.
[05:14] Liam: Yes, tenancy isolation via pinned pools, RBAC and per-tenant quotas. We also support customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
[05:22] Sofia: Sounds promising. Let's outline immediate action items and owners.
[05:26] Maya: Action items: I will share partner deck and security one-pager; Omar will run cost/latency estimate; Ethan will send baseline; Sofia to introduce BD/legal. We'll then schedule a deeper architecture workshop.
[05:38] Priya: Quick clarification
when you talk about quantization recommendations, do you run the evals or we do?
[05:44] Omar: We can collaborate: we run suggested quant profiles and provide test harness; you run your evals and we monitor. We'll tie any regressions to your prompt set.
[05:53] Derek: Great. Anything else on go-to-market collaboration?
[05:56] Maya: We typically do joint webinars and co-marketing once pilot proves out. We'll follow up with partner program details.
[06:04] Sofia: Okay, thanks all.

[06:08] End of main discussion. Additional quick notes (informal):
- Transcription had a few mis-hears: KV cash -> KV cache; LyraGrid sometimes auto-capitalized incorrectly.
- Shared artifacts will be posted to the shared Slack channel and attached to CRM.
